candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company invited applications for 2,00,000 equity shares from the public and received applications for only 1,80,000 shares. Assume the company has received the minimum subscription. For how many shares will the allotment be confirmed, following the treatment of under subscription in the NCERT text?

options.text: 2,00,000 shares, the number for which applications were invited
20,000 shares, the number of shares left unsubscribed
1,80,000 shares, the number of shares actually applied for
1,90,000 shares, the number used in the textbook example

candidate.explanation: Under subscription is a situation where the number of shares applied for is less than the number for which applications were invited. In the textbook example, where 2 lakh shares were offered and applications came for 1,90,000, allotment is confirmed to the shares applied for. Here applications are for 1,80,000 shares, so allotment is confirmed to 1,80,000 shares; 2,00,000 is the number invited, 20,000 is only the shortfall, and 1,90,000 belongs to the textbook example, not to this company.

learning_objective.objective: Explain the treatment of under subscription of shares at allotment.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company issues 10,000 equity shares of nominal value Rs. 50 each at Rs. 56 per share. The amount of premium is credited to a separate account called the Securities Premium Account. What amount is credited to the Securities Premium Account on the issue of these shares?
candidate.explanation: A share issued at an amount more than its nominal value is issued at a premium, so the premium is Rs. 56 - Rs. 50 = Rs. 6 per share. For 10,000 shares this is 10,000 x 6 = Rs. 60,000. Rs. 5,00,000 is 10,000 x 50, the nominal value; Rs. 5,60,000 is 10,000 x 56, the total issue price; Rs. 6,000 is 1,000 x 6, which applies the premium to only 1,000 shares.

learning_objective.objective: Compute the securities premium arising on issue of shares at a premium.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: Satish and Tilak are partners sharing profits equally. During the year, Satish withdrew Rs. 30,000 at the end of each quarter, that is Rs. 1,20,000 in all. Interest on drawings is charged at 8% per annum. Following the NCERT method for fixed amounts withdrawn quarterly, what is the interest on Satish's drawings?
candidate.explanation: When a fixed amount is withdrawn at the end of each quarter, interest is calculated on the total money withdrawn during the year for a period of 4.5 months. Interest = 1,20,000 x 8/100 x 4.5/12 = Rs. 3,600. Rs. 6,000 uses 7.5 months, which applies to withdrawals at the beginning of each quarter; Rs. 4,800 uses 6 months; Rs. 900 applies 4.5 months to only one withdrawal of Rs. 30,000.

learning_objective.objective: Calculate interest on partners' drawings when a fixed amount is withdrawn quarterly.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: X and Y are partners. Z is admitted as a new partner and pays Rs. 30,000 as premium for goodwill directly (privately) to X and Y. Which of the following is the treatment in the books of the firm?

options.text: No entry is passed in the books of the firm
Bank A/c Dr. To Premium for Goodwill A/c, for Rs. 30,000
Bank A/c Dr. To Z's Capital A/c, for Rs. 30,000
Goodwill A/c Dr. To X's and Y's Capital A/cs, for Rs. 30,000

candidate.explanation: If the premium is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, no entry is passed in the books of the firm. The entries debiting Bank A/c apply when the amount is paid through the firm, and the Goodwill A/c entry distributing goodwill to the sacrificing partners belongs to the through-the-firm treatment as well. Here the amount is paid directly, so options B, C and D are not required.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Partnership Accounts - Admission of a Partner
learning_objective.objective: Identify the accounting treatment of premium for goodwill paid privately by a new partner.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company issues debentures that are payable in a lump sum on the expiry of 10 years and that carry a charge on a specific machine held for use in operations. How are these debentures correctly described?

options.text: Secured with a floating charge; redeemable
Secured with a fixed charge; redeemable
Secured with a fixed charge; irredeemable

candidate.explanation: A charge on a specific asset is a fixed charge, and debentures with a charge created on company assets are secured; a floating charge is on the general assets, so A is wrong. Unsecured debentures have no specific charge on assets, so B is wrong. Debentures payable on the expiry of a specific period in lump sum are redeemable, whereas irredeemable debentures carry no undertaking for repayment, so D is wrong.

learning_objective.objective: Classify debentures by security and by tenure.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: The past average profits of a firm work out at Rs. 45,000 and such profits are expected to continue for another four years. Under the Average Profits Method, what is the value of goodwill?
candidate.explanation: Under the Average Profits Method, goodwill is the past average profits multiplied by the number of years of anticipated profits. Because the first year's profit is already being earned, only 3 years remain to be counted, so goodwill = 45,000 x 3 = Rs. 1,35,000.

learning_objective.objective: Value goodwill by the average profits method.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A company offered 5,00,000 shares to the public for subscription. In which of the following situations is the issue a case of over subscription?

options.text: Applications are received for exactly 5,00,000 shares

candidate.explanation: Over subscription arises when applications for more shares are received than the number offered to the public. Applications for 6,00,000 shares exceed the 5,00,000 offered. Applications for exactly 5,00,000 are not more than offered, and applications for 4,50,000 are fewer than offered, which is under subscription.

learning_objective.objective: Distinguish over subscription from under subscription of shares.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: P and Q share profits in the ratio 2 : 1. On dissolution of the firm, the balance sheet shows a General Reserve of Rs. 30,000. How is it transferred to the partners' capital accounts?

options.text: P's Capital Rs. 10,000 and Q's Capital Rs. 20,000
P's Capital Rs. 20,000 and Q's Capital Rs. 10,000
P's Capital Rs. 15,000 and Q's Capital Rs. 15,000

candidate.explanation: Accumulated profits in the form of General Reserve are transferred to the partners' capital accounts in their profit sharing ratio, so P gets 2/3 of 30,000 = Rs. 20,000 and Q gets Rs. 10,000. This reserve is credited only to those partners whose capital accounts show a credit balance, so a partner with a debit balance in his capital account would receive no share of it.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Partnership Accounts - Dissolution of a Firm
learning_objective.objective: Record the transfer of accumulated profits to partners' capital accounts on dissolution.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body: A partner withdrew Rs. 24,000 at the beginning of each quarter during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 10% per annum. Following the NCERT method for fixed amounts withdrawn quarterly, what is the interest on drawings?
candidate.explanation: Total drawings for the year are 24,000 x 4 = Rs. 96,000. For withdrawals at the beginning of each quarter, interest is calculated for 7.5 months. Interest = 96,000 x 10/100 x 7.5/12 = 9,600 x 7.5/12 = Rs. 7,200.

learning_objective.objective: Calculate interest on partners' drawings when a fixed amount is withdrawn quarterly.
